nodes.title: Approval lane, retry 4 of three refused board specs (main ran scripts/approve-generate.mjs --keep-refused from int/r6 3132d629a; n = 3 topics, 5 model calls, $0.0056; $0.0225 of the $0.25 cap spent across all retries): c4-maths-ch05-t01 candidate on attempt 2, c5-maths-ch02-t02 candidate on attempt 1, c5-maths-ch02-t01 refused on both attempts. All 3 refusals carry the same content finding: content_safety_2 on waves.1.title, text 'Teen hisse' (twice) and 'Teen barabar hisse' (once). Outputs on claude/r4-content-candidates 07cf76d25, data/studio-approved/candidates-retry4/. No judge has seen the candidates yet.

The content-safety check on generated board specs flags the romanised Hindi number word 'teen' (three) as the English word: 3 of 3 refusals in retry 4 were this and nothing else. It is a false positive that blocks any title with 'teen' in it (thirds are a class 4-5 topic). Seen only on spec titles; whether it also fires on lesson text or kits was not measured.

Generated board specs write numbers as digits in titles and labels ('3 hisse'), never as a romanised number word; the generation `how` says so and approve-check names the cause when a title fails on a number word. The content-safety check itself is not changed now (owner: existing safety code is frozen until the pre-launch safety pass). Reverse if: the pre-launch safety pass makes the check language-aware, or digits in titles read worse to children than the word in a judged sample.

For the pre-launch safety pass: make the content check language-aware so romanised Hindi number words ('teen', and check 'das', 'char', 'saat', 'nau', 'sau') are not read as English, and measure how often it fires on kits, scripts and teacher lines. Not to be done before that pass (safety code frozen).
